A year in a minute

A year of orbits in a minute. Leaving puts the clock back and you back to Earth.

Open the trip: A year in a minute

Everything inside Mars, going round

Every second here is six days, so Mercury goes round the Sun in fifteen seconds and the Earth in a minute. Each planet is a dot drawn far larger than it is, on the path it really follows.

The Earth, and the Moon going round it

The Moon goes round the Earth every 27.3 days, which here is four and a half seconds. The camera is riding along with the Earth at thirty kilometres a second, so it is everything farther away that seems to drift.

Mercury, four laps to our one

Mercury goes round the Sun in 88 days, four times in each of our years, at 47 kilometres a second. The camera is following it, so it is the Sun that seems to wheel round behind.

Jupiter, which takes twelve of our years

Jupiter is five times as far from the Sun as we are and needs almost twelve of our years to go round once. While the Earth goes round one time, Jupiter covers a twelfth of its path.

Everything is drawn where it really is, from the planets’ own orbits (astronomy-engine).
